questions.stem: Find the area of a rectangle 12 cm long and 7 cm wide.
questions.explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times breadth, so $12 \times 7 = 84$ cm². The unit is cm² because two lengths were multiplied together.

distractorRationale.a: This is the perimeter, $2(12 + 7)$, not the area
distractorRationale.c: Added the two dimensions instead of multiplying
distractorRationale.d: Doubled the area, perhaps by also applying the perimeter formula's factor of 2

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30$ cm². A triangle is exactly half the rectangle that encloses it, which is where the $\frac{1}{2}$ comes from.

distractorRationale.a: Added the base and height instead of multiplying
distractorRationale.c: Forgot to halve the product
distractorRationale.d: Doubled instead of halving

questions.stem: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm, taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: Circumference is $2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 44$ cm. The radius of 7 cancels with the denominator, which is why $\frac{22}{7}$ is convenient here.

distractorRationale.c: This is the area in cm², using $\pi r^2$ rather than the circumference
distractorRationale.d: Treated the 7 as a diameter and doubled it as well

questions.stem: Find the area of a circle of radius 14 cm, taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: Area is $\pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 196 = 22 \times 28 = 616$ cm². Remember to square the radius before multiplying by π.

distractorRationale.b: Used the radius once instead of squaring it, then doubled
distractorRationale.d: Squared the diameter instead of the radius, then halved

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides of 8 cm and 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The area is $\frac{1}{2}(a + b)h = \frac{1}{2}(8 + 12) \times 5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5 = 50$ cm². The formula averages the two parallel sides, then multiplies by the height.

distractorRationale.a: Used only the 8 cm side as the base
distractorRationale.c: Forgot the factor of one half
distractorRationale.d: Halved the height as well as the sum of the parallel sides

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm and a perpendicular height of 4 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height, $9 \times 4 = 36$ cm². There is no halving here, unlike the triangle formula, because a parallelogram is made of two identical triangles.

distractorRationale.b: Halved the product, using the triangle formula by mistake
distractorRationale.c: This is the perimeter if the slant side were 4 cm, not the area

questions.stem: The area of a square is 144 cm². Find its perimeter in centimetres. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: The side of the square is $\sqrt{144} = 12$ cm. The perimeter is four times the side, so $4 \times 12 = 48$ cm. You must find the side length before you can find the perimeter.

questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 21 cm. Find its circumference, taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
questions.explanation: With the diameter given, use $C = \pi d = \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = 66$ cm. If you prefer $2\pi r$, halve the diameter first to get $r = 10.5$ cm, which gives the same 66 cm.

distractorRationale.a: Used the radius 10.5 in $\pi d$ instead of the diameter
distractorRationale.c: Applied $2\pi d$, doubling when the diameter was already given
distractorRationale.d: This is the area in cm², not the circumference

questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 46 cm and its length is 14 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: From $2(l + b) = 46$ we get $l + b = 23$, so the width is $23 - 14 = 9$ cm. The area is then $14 \times 9 = 126$ cm².

distractorRationale.b: Used a width of 16 cm from $46 - 14 - 16$ mis-set up
distractorRationale.c: Took the width as 32 cm by subtracting 14 from 46 directly
distractorRationale.d: Multiplied the length by the whole perimeter minus the length, without halving first

questions.stem: A farm has an area of 0.6 hectares. Express this area in square metres.
questions.explanation: One hectare is $10\,000$ m², which is the area of a square of side 100 m. So $0.6 \times 10\,000 = 6000$ m².

distractorRationale.c: Multiplied by 100 000 instead of 10 000
distractorRationale.d: Used 100 m² per hectare, confusing the area factor with the length factor
